answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before earning reputation or receiving work. A challenge reveals whether an identity double-signs or breaks a contract; proof lets the system burn its stake and lower its reputation. Creating a thousand names then requires a thousand funded deposits, and a detected attack destroys capital, so identities are costly rather than free. The ferrous lock can weather a gale of fake accounts, though it cannot stop an ocean of attackers who can afford the deposits.
